title: A structurally dynamic N-terminal helix is a key functional determinant in staphylococcal complement inhibitor (SCIN) proteins.
experiment: 15N longitudinal (R1, inversion-recovery) and transverse (R2, CPMG) relaxation and steady-state 15N-1H NOE at 599.7 MHz (14.1 T)
buffer: argon-saturated d13-MES (pH 6.9), 5% (v/v) D2O, 0.2 mM 3-(trimethylsilyl)-1-propane-sulfonic acid, 1 mM NaN3
construct_or_mutation: full-length unbound SCIN-A (S. aureus strain Mu50, 85 residues)
other_conditions: protein concentration: 800 uM; 63 of 85 well-resolved 1H-15N resonances analyzed (78 of 85 assigned); overall 15N-1H NOE = 0.69 ± 0.02 vs N-terminal residues 15N-1H NOE = 0.33 ± 0.08; overall R1 = 1.48 ± 0.25 Hz; N-terminal R2 and R2/R1 ratios substantially lower than core; 仅图示: per-residue R1, R2, 15N-1H NOE, and R2/R1 in Fig. 2C and unavailable supplemental Table S1
related_structures: 3OHX (SCIN-A crystal structure chain M); 2WIN ((SCIN-A·C3bBb)2 pseudodimer crystal structure); 2A73 (native human C3 crystal structure)
author_claim: 15N R1, R2, and steady-state 15N-1H NOE relaxation measurements at 599.7 MHz (30 °C, pH 6.9, 800 uM) show that unbound full-length SCIN-A combines a rigid helical bundle core (overall 15N-1H NOE = 0.69 ± 0.02, R1 = 1.48 ± 0.25 Hz) with fast ns-ps backbone flexibility and dynamic sequential order/disorder exchange in its N-terminal residues (15N-1H NOE = 0.33 ± 0.08 and substantially lower R2 and R2/R1 ratios).
anchor: summary of 15N relaxation longitudinal (R1) and transverse (R2) relaxation rates along with 15N-1H NOE values for SCIN-A and SCIN-B. R2/R1 ratios are presented as a measure of site-specific rotational diffusion motion.
locator: Fig. 2C (仅图示); Results, The N-terminal Regions of SCIN Proteins Are Flexible in Solution; supplemental Table S1 (仅图示); conditions: Experimental Procedures, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
caveat_note: Paper-vs-deposit-card discrepancy: Experimental Procedures states 'All NMR data were collected at 30 °C', whereas BMRB 18772 / sheet card lists bmrb_temperature = 273 K and sheet_temperature_K = 273.0 (0 °C). Protein identity (SCIN-A, 85 residues), concentration (800 uM), pH (6.9), D2O (5%), and field (599.7 MHz vs card 600 MHz) match BMRB 18772, while paper additionally specifies argon-saturated d13-MES, 0.2 mM DSS, and 1 mM NaN3 omitted from bmrb_sample_components; BMRB 18772 is not cited by accession number in paper.txt. CPMG here denotes standard transverse R2 measurement, not relaxation dispersion. Exact N-terminal residue numbers and per-residue values are only in Fig. 2C and unavailable supplemental Table S1.

title: A structurally dynamic N-terminal helix is a key functional determinant in staphylococcal complement inhibitor (SCIN) proteins.
experiment: 13Calpha and 13CO secondary chemical shift (Delta_delta_rc <= 0.50 ppm) analysis from 3D triple-resonance NMR spectra at 599.7 MHz (14.1 T)
buffer: argon-saturated d13-MES (pH 6.9), 5% (v/v) D2O, 0.2 mM 3-(trimethylsilyl)-1-propane-sulfonic acid, 1 mM NaN3
construct_or_mutation: full-length unbound SCIN-A (S. aureus strain Mu50, 85 residues)
other_conditions: protein concentration: 800 uM; >90% of 13CO, 13Calpha, and 13Cbeta resonances assigned; 仅图示: complete residue map with 13Calpha Delta_delta_rc <= 0.50 ppm colored red on chain M of 3OHX in Fig. 2A
related_structures: 3OHX (SCIN-A crystal structure chain M); 2WIN ((SCIN-A·C3bBb)2 pseudodimer crystal structure); 2A73 (native human C3 crystal structure)
author_claim: Comparison of observed 13CO and 13Calpha chemical shifts with random coil values for unbound SCIN-A indicates variable ensemble-averaged alpha-helical secondary structure increasing progressively inward from the N-terminus (N-terminal helix starting near N8, breaking at E25, resuming to a 3-residue loop starting at G34), along with coil/loop shifts at interhelical linkers, the C-terminus, and an unexpected 2-residue deviation in helix 3 at I73/Y74.
anchor: Values of 13C␣ chemical shift were compared with random coil chemical shifts, and resulting difference values ⱕ0.50 ppm were mapped in red onto the crystal structures of SCIN-A and SCIN-B(4 – 85).
locator: Fig. 2A (仅图示); Results, The N-terminal Regions of SCIN Proteins Are Flexible in Solution; conditions: Experimental Procedures, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy
caveat_note: Paper-vs-deposit-card discrepancy: paper reports 30 °C for all NMR experiments whereas BMRB 18772 / sheet card lists 273 K (273.0 K); SCIN-A concentration (800 uM), pH (6.9), D2O (5%), and field (~600 MHz) match. Only boundary/deviation residues N8, E25, G34, I73, and Y74 are named in text; all other red-mapped positions with 13Calpha Delta_delta_rc <= 0.50 ppm are shown only in Fig. 2A.

title: A structurally dynamic N-terminal helix is a key functional determinant in staphylococcal complement inhibitor (SCIN) proteins.
experiment: X-ray crystal structure comparison and main-chain B-factor analysis (BAVERAGE) of full-length SCIN-B (4H6I, 3.1 Å, C222) and SCIN-B(4-85) (4H6H, 2.5 Å, P32)
buffer: protein in 10 mM Tris (pH 7.4), 50 mM NaCl; SCIN-B (4H6I) precipitant: 0.2 M ammonium sulfate, 30% (w/v) PEG 8,000 (5% glycerol cryoprotectant); SCIN-B(4-85) (4H6H) precipitant: 0.1 M Tris (pH 8.5), 8% (w/v) PEG 8,000 (30% glycerol cryoprotectant)
construct_or_mutation: full-length SCIN-B and N-terminal truncation mutant SCIN-B(4-85) (S. aureus strain Mu50 paralog)
other_conditions: crystals flash-cooled in liquid nitrogen for X-ray diffraction; 4H6I: 3 molecules/ASU, mean B-factors = 68.06 Å2; 4H6H: 4 molecules/ASU, mean B-factors = 43.98 Å2; per-residue B-factors plotted in unavailable supplemental Fig. S2
alt_state_structure: 4H6I: N-terminal random coil / non-classical secondary structure conformation of full-length SCIN-B, residues E9-Q19 (Fig. 1A, Table 1); 4H6H: N-terminal alpha-helical conformation of SCIN-B(4-85) (Fig. 1B, Table 1)
author_claim: Crystallographic comparison of full-length SCIN-B (4H6I) and SCIN-B(4-85) (4H6H) with SCIN-B(18-85) (3T49) reveals a conserved three-helix bundle core alongside a helix-to-coil transition in the N-terminal region (alpha-helical in 4H6H vs non-classical coil from Q19 to E9 with residues 1-8 unmodeled in 4H6I) and elevated N-terminal main-chain B-factors in both crystal structures including helical 4H6H.
anchor: FIGURE 1. Crystal structures of SCIN-B reveal a flexible N-terminal region.
locator: Fig. 1; Table 1; Results, Crystal Structures of SCIN-B Reveal a Flexible N-terminal Region; supplemental Fig. S2; conditions: Experimental Procedures, Crystallization, X-ray Diffraction Data Collection, Structure Solution, and Refinement
caveat_note: Homolog row (SCIN-B paralog of target SCIN-A). Temperature 4 °C is the crystal growth temperature; X-ray diffraction data were collected after cryoprotection and flash cooling in liquid nitrogen (cryo data-collection temperature not numerically stated). PISA crystal-contact analysis shows N-terminal residues in SCIN-B(4-85) (4H6H, P32) make nearly twice as many crystallographic contacts as in full-length SCIN-B (4H6I, C222), which may favor helix in 4H6H vs coil in 4H6I, though unexpectedly elevated N-terminal B-factors in helical 4H6H and solution NMR independently support intrinsic N-terminal flexibility.
